event.title: Karoline Leavitt to Depart as White House Press Secretary
event.canonical_title: Karoline Leavitt to Depart as White House Press Secretary
event.summary: Karoline Leavitt will step down from her role as White House press secretary at the end of the month, as announced by President Donald Trump. Leavitt described her decision as bittersweet, having recently returned to work after the birth of her second child. She is noted for being the youngest person to hold the position and will continue as a senior advisor following her departure.

event_overview.title: About White House Press Secretary
event_overview.subject: White House Press Secretary
event_overview.summary: This event concerns a planned leadership change in the White House Press Secretary’s Office, the office that communicates the president’s activities and agenda to the media. Karoline Leavitt has held the role during President Donald Trump’s second administration; the reported departure sets up a White House decision on her successor rather than a Senate-confirmed vacancy.

facts.label: Role and institution
facts.value: The White House describes the Press Secretary’s Office as part of the Executive Office of the President; the press secretary provides media briefings on the president’s activities and agenda.

facts.label: Officeholder and start date
facts.value: Karoline Leavitt’s public financial disclosure identifies her White House position as Press Secretary and lists January 20, 2025, as her appointment date. A White House announcement also identified her as an Assistant to the President and Press Secretary.

facts.label: Stated communications function
facts.value: The White House Press Office works with media organizations worldwide, while the Office of Communications plans and advances the president’s core messaging; the press secretary is the administration’s principal public briefing official within that structure.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the announced departure and immediate discussion of possible succession, not every White House briefing, personnel development, or any later formal successor appointment.
